concepts.hypothesis: Expanding the parser/canonicalizer faster than the owner-fixed executable semantic contract creates a high-risk zone where the evaluator may silently inherit Python host semantics for newly accepted constructs. Every newly parseable semantic construct therefore needs an explicit semantic owner, effect/type boundary and differential/metamorphic falsifier before executable promotion.
concepts.counterhypothesis: Fail-closed evaluator coverage plus ordinary corpus tests are sufficient; a separate per-construct semantic-contract ledger adds bureaucracy without catching more bugs.
decisive_tests: For each syntax/AST node introduced by #314, classify EXECUTABLE_DEFINED, PARSE_ONLY_FAIL_CLOSED or FORBIDDEN; no implicit fourth state.
Mutation-test each executable construct with at least one semantics-changing mutant and require the relevant gate to reject it.
Track parser coverage separately from executable semantic coverage so 90% parse coverage cannot be read as 90% language implementation.

concepts.hypothesis: Python reference slices remain valuable after the Clay-native mandate if they are explicitly typed as diagnostic baselines, cannot mint target-implementation progress credit, and every target successor is differentially compared against them under the same controls.
concepts.counterhypothesis: Keeping reference Python cognition encourages semantic drift and should be deleted once ClayCode execution exists.
decisive_tests: Build the same four-arm PR #312 loop semantics in Clay/ClayCode and compare link-by-link receipts against the Python baseline.
Lesion the Python scaffold from the target runtime; final target behavior must remain unchanged except for test tooling.
Audit packaging/binary inputs to prove diagnostic reference modules are not runtime semantic dependencies.
